### Added
- **Prompt templates** (#52, added in #56). A request that starts with `/<name>` is replaced by the template of that name, with its arguments filled in (`$1`, `$ARGUMENTS`, `$@`, `${@:N[:L]}`, and `${ARGUMENTS:-default}`). Templates come from the `pi.prompts` of extension packages, from `.pi/prompts` in the repository (only with `trust_project`), and from `<agent_dir>/prompts`. If two templates have the same name, the first one wins. Templates apply to the first request, to follow-ups, and to `prompt` in direct and `pr_number` runs. The log shows what was typed and which template was used. See [Prompt templates](https://github.com/cv/pi-action/blob/v2.4.0/docs/prompts.md#prompt-templates) and [Prompt templates from the repository](https://github.com/cv/pi-action/blob/v2.4.0/docs/security.md#prompt-templates-from-the-repository).
- **Choose the tools that pi can use** (#52, added in #56). Two new inputs: `exclude_tools` turns tools off completely, and `model_tools_hidden` keeps tools away from the model, but other tools (such as pit's `tools.*`) can still call them. Both take names or `*` globs. A name that matches nothing gives a warning, and the run fails if the model has no tools left. The `🤖` line in the log lists the tools that the model gets. See [Tools the model sees](https://github.com/cv/pi-action/blob/v2.4.0/docs/extensions.md#tools-the-model-sees).
- **Extensions can replace tools** (#52, added in #56). If a pi-durable extension registers a tool with the same name as an earlier tool, the later tool replaces it, as with pi's `registerTool`. The log says which extension replaced which tool. See [Override tools and sections](https://github.com/cv/pi-action/blob/v2.4.0/docs/extensions.md#override-tools-and-sections).


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/cv/pi-action/compare/v2.3.0...v2.4.0
